title: Systems Design, Systems Thinking & Systems Engineering — Iceberg Knowledge Foundation
primary_research_workflow: EFT: Exa discovery -> Firecrawl extraction -> TinyFish page/PDF extraction -> cross-check, deduplicate, classify and synthesize. Firecrawl account 1 was exhausted; account 2 was ineligible for Firecrawl execution; account 3 was used successfully until credits became constrained. TinyFish account links supported targeted batches. All source statuses and extraction limitations are recorded in DEEP_SCRAPE_AUDIT.csv.
status: Expanded research/content foundation; no claim of global exhaustiveness, credential endorsement, regulatory approval, or production website.
notes: Current snapshot date: 5 November 2026. Check standards, credential rules, software tools and regulatory adoption with their issuers before use.
User-supplied course screenshots are summarized in 49_USER_COURSE_MATERIALS_CROSSWALK.md; some screenshot content was cut off.
The visible hours in user-supplied course snippets are syllabus durations, not validated mastery or credential equivalence.
User-supplied Dropbox source remains retained but uninspected.
Normative standards may be licensed/paywalled; the repository links and summarizes scope rather than reproducing the normative text.
Source register distinguishes primary, secondary, commercial, private, access-limited, discovery-only and unverified sources.
Domain-specific regulated engineering requires qualified practitioners and jurisdiction-specific interpretation.

The repository includes separate engineering tracks for systems science, systems engineering, software/enterprise architecture, assurance, security, safety, human systems, CPS/control, OR, product support and sustainability.

Documents 61-81 added deeper research on systems methods, mission engineering, requirements evidence, architecture governance, distributed correctness, data contracts, PRA/CCF/PoF, STPA, security, formal methods, HSI, CPS, OR, sector safety, incident forensics, agentic AI, RCM/IPS and specialist exercises.

Documents 82-95 add assurance-case argumentation, SoS governance, architecture frameworks, configuration/digital thread, product-line variability, HRA, uncertainty/value of information, value engineering, data-platform correctness, human-machine teaming, regulatory evidence chains, incident causal learning and an integrated capstone.
DEEP_SCRAPE_AUDIT.csv differentiates full fetch, targeted extraction, partial, discovery-only, blocked/unreachable and gated sources. A source record is not proof that full content was reviewed.
DEEP_COVERAGE_MATRIX.csv describes current depth and residual gaps across the research domains.
The DoW System of Systems Engineering Guidebook (September 2026) and NATO NAF 4.1 (March 2026) were included as current source material in this snapshot.
NASA-STD-0005 is marked inactive for new design; do not present it as a current NASA mandate.
ISO/IEC/IEEE 21839 edition 2 was listed as under publication on 5 November 2026; the 2019 edition remains the published record cited here.
Some incident reports (notably NTSB AIR-25-04, Ariane 501 and Bank of England RTGS) remain discovery-only or not fully extracted; see the audit.
Some sector standards are only mapped at a high level; full applicability depends on jurisdiction, intended use, regulator, contract and certification basis.
Exercises are design/research prompts; they have not been executed, formally verified, independently graded or certified.

Documents 96-102 add decision-analysis and trade-study methods, NASA lifecycle review gates under NPR 7123.1D, SEMP and technical planning, DoD IMP/IMS integration, ISO 42030 architecture evaluation, operational SLI/SLO/error-budget practice, RCM task selection and MBSE model assurance.

practice_prompts.csv now includes advanced exercises P46-P65 covering GSN, SoS, DoDAF/UAF/NAF, digital thread, product lines, HRA, uncertainty/VOI, value engineering, data contracts, human-machine teaming, sector assurance, incident forensics, provenance, trade studies, reviews, SEMP/IMP/IMS, architecture evaluation, SLOs, RCM and model assurance.

Documents 103-110 extend the foundation into system dynamics model validation, lifecycle V&V and independence, model/simulation credibility, environmental qualification, integrated system safety, sector assurance, standards revision tracking and living FMECA.

Current-status corrections recorded as of 2026-11-05: IEC 61508-1:2026 is FDIS/PRV in ballot (not final published Edition 3); ISO/IEC/IEEE DIS 29148 Edition 3 is still a draft; ISO/IEC/IEEE 21839 Edition 2 is under publication; FDA medical-device cybersecurity guidance issued 2026-02-03 supersedes the 2025 guidance.

New extraction batch used TinyFish for NASA System Safety Handbook Volumes 1 and 2, STPA Primer, NASA-HDBK-1009A, GSFC-HDBK-8004, current FDA 2026 guidance, ISO automotive/medical/architecture records and FAA references. The 2025 NASA risk-informed safety-case PDF remained target_unreachable; see audit.

Document 111 adds quantitative reliability science: Weibull and exponential lifetime models, right/interval censoring, MLE, reliability demonstration confidence bounds, Crow-AMSAA reliability growth, accelerated-life models, Physics of Failure, IEC 61709 stress conversion and ISO 14224 data governance.

Documents 112-118 add repairable-system HPP/NHPP and Markov dependability, prognostics/PHM and ISO 13381-1:2025, manufacturing/workmanship and EEE parts assurance, DMSMS/obsolescence, measurement and leading indicators, integrated product support/LORA, and Bayesian/RIDM/robust decisions. Latest coverage/audit counts are recalculated after writing.

The official DLA DMSMS page states SD-22 was updated January 2026, but the January 2026 PDF was not fetched; the March 2024 PDF surfaced in search is a working draft and is not treated as current text.
ISO 13381-1:2025 Edition 3 was verified as the current published prognostics standard, replacing withdrawn 2015 Edition 2.

Some supportability source PDFs (IPS Element Guidebook, DoDI 5000.91 and PSM Guidebook) could not be retrieved during this pass; their entries distinguish official page/metadata discovery from full-text extraction.
